Base outfit: several days (the Grave Danger Quest has bosses with a 20 h cooldown). Addons: minutes if you buy both items on the Market; many attempts if you hunt them yourself (very rare drops)

The {wiki:Hand of the Inquisition Outfits|Hand of the Inquisition Outfits} belong to the {wiki:Grave Danger Quest|Grave Danger Quest}: you receive the base outfit when you defeat {creature:King Zelos} and report to {npc:Jack Springer}, in Thais. The first addon is obtained by using a {item:Final Judgement}, which drops (very rarely) from five bosses of the Grave Danger graves; the second addon by using a {item:Shadow Cowl}, which only King Zelos drops. Both items can also be bought on the Market. With both addons you earn the achievement **Inquisition's Arm**.
Help the Inquisition defeat the lich knights and find rare treasures you can wear to show our success.

The {item:Final Judgement} and the {item:Shadow Cowl} are **tradeable** (Market) and no NPC buys or sells them. If you don't want to hunt the bosses, buy them from other players: the effect is the same. The base outfit, however, always requires the completed Grave Danger Quest.

The {item:Final Judgement} drops from **five** different bosses ({creature:Count Vlarkorth}, {creature:Lord Azaram}, {creature:Earl Osam}, {creature:Sir Baeloc} and {creature:Duke Krule}), each with its own **20-hour** cooldown. Killing all five whenever the cooldown ends gives you five chances a day.

**Fire** is the best element against almost all these bosses ({creature:Count Vlarkorth} is the exception: use Death). Against most of them you should avoid Death (on Sir Baeloc and Sir Nictros, Death even heals them).
Several bosses apply *Lesser Hex* (cuts the healing received) and King Zelos applies *Greater Hex* (lowers maximum health to 40%). Blockers should always watch the status bar.
1. Base outfit: complete the Grave Danger Quest

The base outfit is the final reward of the {wiki:Grave Danger Quest|Grave Danger Quest}. Here you have a summary of everything you need to do and the final fight with {creature:King Zelos} (which you repeat for the {item:Shadow Cowl}). The full routes to each of the 12 graves are in that quest's guide; the five grave bosses that drop the {item:Final Judgement} are explained, with the way there and back, in section 2.

Travel to **Thais** (by boat: to the captain in your city say {key:hi}, {key:thais} and {key:yes}; you arrive at {npc:Captain Bluebear}'s harbour). The Inquisition headquarters is beneath the city: go down here {coord:32317,32269,7} and find {npc:Jack Springer} in a room **two floors below** ground. To leave, go back up the same stairs to the street.
Way down to the Inquisition headquarters

Talk to {npc:Jack Springer}: say {key:hi} and {key:mission}. He explains the plan of the Shiron'Fal (the *legion*) to resurrect fallen knights as lich-knights. Continue with these words, in this order: {key:urgency}, {key:start}, {key:source}, {key:events}, {key:more}, {key:many}, {key:iceberg}, {key:hand}, {key:predates}, {key:language}, {key:legion}, {key:goal}, {key:stopped}, {key:clashes}, {key:hurry}, {key:problem}, {key:knights}, {key:lich}, {key:scheme}, {key:threats}, {key:rituals}, {key:purge} and, finally, {key:late}.
If you don't want to hear the whole story, just say {key:hi} and {key:late}: that is the word that gives you the mission.
Buying the Vial of Potent Holy Water

Still with {npc:Jack Springer}, say {key:trade} and buy the {item:Vial of Potent Holy Water} (100 gp each). If you need more, ask for {key:trade} again. If you forget where the graves are, say {key:report} and then {key:locations}: he gives you the list.

You have to visit **12 graves** of fallen knights, in any order. Six only need a visit and the Holy Water (Dark Cathedral, Femor Hills, Kilmaresh, Vengoth, Orclands and Folda); the others have bosses that you face with teams of **up to 5 players** and that you can repeat every **20 hours**. The last column says how you get to each grave and how you get back; the {wiki:Grave Danger Quest|Grave Danger Quest} guide has each route step by step.

{npc:Nielson}, **north-west** of Carlin: {key:hi}, {key:folda}, {key:yes} (20 gp); you arrive at the Folda dock, next to {npc:Svenson}. Leave the mountain the same way and say {key:hi}, {key:tibia}, {key:yes} to Svenson (free trip back to the mainland)
Each grave boss has a **20-hour** cooldown. Plan the quest over several days and take the chance to try for the {item:Final Judgement} on each one straight away (section 2).

This is the longest grave. Travel by boat to **Ankrahmun** (for example from Venore, Darashia or Edron: {key:hi}, {key:ankrahmun}, {key:yes}; you arrive at {npc:Captain Sinbeard}). The {wiki:Cobra Bastion} is on an island **north-east** of the Ankrahmun desert ({coord:33301,32647,7}) and only players of level 250+ can enter; the wiki does not describe the exact path to the entrance, so use the coordinate on the map to find your way. Go up the ramp in the **south** part of the bastion and then two more floors: on the 3rd floor, in the **south-east** room, is {creature:Gaffir}. Defeat him to gain access to the basement. Go back to the ground floor, down to the basement and follow the corridors on the **west** side, always heading **south**: in the southernmost room is the {creature:Custodian}. The grave is in the room **north** of the Custodian: use the {item:Vial of Potent Holy Water} on it. To leave, go back through the same corridors and stairs to the bastion entrance and return to Ankrahmun, where {npc:Captain Sinbeard} takes you to Darashia, Venore, Edron, Liberty Bay, Port Hope or Yalahar.

For Grave Danger you don't need to unlock the rest of the bastion or kill {creature:Scarlett Etzel}, but she drops valuable equipment. The rest of the access (Guard Captain Quaid and the chess puzzle with the {item:Cheesy Figurine}) is in the {wiki:Grave Danger Quest|Grave Danger Quest} guide.
Since 18 April 2023 it is no longer viable to stand inside the fire walls where Gaffir and {creature:Guard Captain Quaid} spawn while you kill them.

With the 12 graves sanctified, go back to the Inquisition headquarters in Thais (step 1) and talk to {npc:Jack Springer}: {key:hi}, {key:report}, {key:ultimate} and {key:threat}. He sends you to the {wiki:Isle of the Kings|Isle of the Kings}, where the grave of the fallen king **Zelos** is hidden; the cultists want to resurrect him with the help of at least four lich-knights.
Get to the Isle of the Kings

Travel to **Carlin** (by boat: to the captain in your city say {key:hi}, {key:carlin} and {key:yes}; you arrive at {npc:Captain Greyhound}'s harbour). Go to {npc:Dalbrect}'s hut and boat, at the harbour **north and west** of the city (north of the {wiki:Ghostlands}). Say {key:hi}, {key:passage} and {key:yes}: he takes you to the {wiki:Isle of the Kings} for 10 gp, if you are already his friend (Family Brooch from {wiki:The White Raven Monastery Quest}).
Dalbrect (boat to the Isle of the Kings)
Going down to King Zelos's sealed door

On the island, go to the large monks' building (on the **east** side). If you haven't done it yet in {wiki:The White Raven Monastery Quest|White Raven Monastery Quest}, talk to Abbot {npc:Costello}: {key:hi}, {key:Fugio} and {key:yes}. From then on you can open the *warded doors* of the catacombs. The catacombs entrance is in that same building: go down to **floor -1**, where access to King Zelos is behind a sealed door, here {coord:32172,31922,8}. Go through the door to reach the ritual area, with the rooms of the four lich-knights and the king.

Don't go up to the 3rd floor of the building (the monks' restricted area, above the library): if you go in there, {npc:Dalbrect} and {npc:Captain Jack} stop transporting you until you pay Costello the fine ({key:absolution}; up to 10,000 gp, depending on your level).
Map of floor -1 of the Isle of the Kings
Fight plan: 4 lich-knights and the king

The fight is for **up to 10 players** (a full team is recommended) and you have **24 minutes** to kill {creature:King Zelos} before you are kicked out of the room. First the team has to kill the **4 lich-knights** performing the ritual to resurrect the king. Each one is in a different room; you can move freely between rooms and kill them in any order. The longer you take, the stronger the king becomes: if you don't kill all four within about **12 minutes**, he becomes too strong or even immune to all damage. The most common order:
2 to 3 players (with a Knight and a Druid)
The rest of the team, at the same time as the Red Knight
Through the teleport in the centre of the north corridor {coord:33443,31545,13}
Avoid **Death** damage against the four lich-knights and against the king.

With {creature:Rewar the Bloody} are {creature:Risen Soldier|Risen Soldiers} and {creature:Fetter|Fetters}. The boss **is only vulnerable when no Fetters are alive**: the goal is to kill them as fast as possible and, when the boss becomes vulnerable, hit him with everything before he becomes immune again. Positioning: **four players** surround the centre tile of the room, where the boss appears every time he changes form (Knights on the sides, shooters, preferably Paladins, to the north and south, so the boss does not face them). The other **six** stand around the spots where the Fetters spawn (west, east and north/south of each one; you can see the blue spawn effect), so they can only move back and forth: Sorcerers preferably to the north and south (waves), Druids on the sides ({spell:Mass Healing} for those nearby). That way all the shooters can cast {item:Great Fireball Rune|Great Fireball Runes} on the exact centre of the room and hit the Fetters and the boss at the same time; when the boss is clearly vulnerable, the mages use their waves on him.
Try to finish this part in **under 6 minutes**, otherwise it will be very hard to kill King Zelos in time. Use Fire on the Fetters; avoid Death.

It is the easiest of the four: 2 or 3 players are enough, and splitting the team saves a lot of time. {creature:The Red Knight} **only takes Drown damage**, which comes from killing the {creature:Vampiric Blood|Vampiric Bloods} around him. Kill the Vampiric Bloods **next to** the boss until he dies. Equip Drown protection and don't use Death.
The {creature:Risen Soldier|Risen Soldiers} can be dangerous because there are few players here, so it may be safer to bring a 3rd player.

At first you just attack {creature:Magnor Mournbringer}. When he dies, he splits into 4 {creature:Shard of Magnor|Shards of Magnor}, which you also have to kill. The Shards share the same health, so you can attack just one of them. When they die, they **explode** and each deals about 2000 **Life Drain** damage. To avoid taking all the damage, split them into two groups of two, so the blockers don't get hit by all four explosions. Equip protection against Earth and Life Drain and avoid Death.
The players who killed the Red Knight should arrive when Magnor is almost dead: then the whole team moves on to the north-west corner.

You can attack {creature:Nargol the Impaler} with **Fire** from the start, with no special mechanics (don't use Death on him). When he dies, a {creature:Regenerating Mass} appears in the centre of the room and **you have 30 seconds to kill it**. If you fail, Nargol respawns with full health. A good strategy is to trap the boss in the centre of the room with players and summoned {creature:Fire Elemental|Fire Elementals}: that way the Regenerating Mass spawns already trapped and everyone can focus their damage on it.
Use all the damage you have on the Regenerating Mass: failing this boss once will probably ruin the whole fight and leave King Zelos immortal.

With the four lich-knights dead, enter the teleport in the centre of the **north** corridor to reach {creature:King Zelos}'s room (480,000 HP). The biggest danger is *Greater Hex*, which reduces the target's total health to **40%** of the maximum and comes from the king's **beam**: the blockers should **always stand diagonal** to him. Anyone hit by Greater Hex can remove it by stepping on the vortex in the centre of the room, but that spawns an {creature:Unleashed Hex}, which is quite strong; it is often better for the team to communicate and focus healing on the Knight. If the king is blocked next to the **west** wall, the blocker can keep him facing the wall (and not the team) and change position quickly if the boss moves. There are 3 {creature:Risen Soldier|Risen Soldiers} in the room: a second Knight (or the shooters, preferably Paladins) blocks them; there is no point killing them, because they respawn quickly. The shooters attack the king **only with Fire**, preferably {item:Fireball Rune|Fireball Runes} (maximum single-target damage).
Equip protection against **Death** and don't use Death on him. The king also has a death ring that grows every second (1200–2000) and melee up to 2700.
If the four lich-knights died quickly, the king is weak enough to be killed in time.
75,000 experience and King Zelos's loot (may include the {item:Shadow Cowl}, see section 3)
Leave the Isle of the Kings

If you don't kill the king within 24 minutes, you are kicked out of the room. The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room: once you are out of it, go back through the sealed door on floor -1 ({coord:32172,31922,8}), climb up the catacombs to the monks' building and go to the boat moored at the island. Say {key:hi} and {key:tibia} to {npc:Captain Jack}: he takes you back to the mainland, to the Carlin side (according to the wiki, he only does so if {npc:Costello} has already given you permission; see the step “Going down to King Zelos's sealed door”). From there take {npc:Captain Greyhound}'s boat to **Thais** ({key:hi}, {key:thais}, {key:yes}).

Go back to the Inquisition headquarters in Thais (step 1) and report to {npc:Jack Springer} ({key:hi}, {key:report}). You receive the **base outfit** of the Hand of the Inquisition Outfits and the **Inquisition's Hand** achievement (3 points): *"You defeated the Lich Knights and became the hand of the Inquisition, allowed to wear their special garb."*
Official artwork of the outfit, when it was still called Tomb Assassin

The wiki does not transcribe this last conversation: it only says that, after defeating King Zelos, you go back to Jack Springer to receive the rewards. Use {key:report}, the word he uses in the other reports.
Hand of the Inquisition Outfit (base) and Inquisition's Hand achievement

The {item:Final Judgement} can only be obtained as a (very rare) drop from five of the Grave Danger Quest grave bosses. Either you buy it on the Market, or you hunt the bosses with your team (up to 5 players, 20-hour cooldown each).
Quick option: buy on the Market

Search for **Final Judgement** on the Market of any depot and buy it. No NPC sells or buys it. The wiki estimates its value at between **40,000,000 and 60,000,000 gp**. If you buy it, skip to the step “Using the Final Judgement”.
The price is negotiated between players; compare the offers before buying.
Any of these five bosses can drop the {item:Final Judgement}. All give **55,000** experience, have a **20-hour** cooldown and allow teams of **up to 5 players**.

In the wiki's statistics, Count Vlarkorth dropped the Final Judgement in about **2%** of kills; for the other four it is listed in the loot but has not even appeared in the collected samples (it is even rarer). Expect many attempts.
Getting to the Edron grave (Count Vlarkorth)

Travel to **Edron** (by boat: to the captain in your city say {key:hi}, {key:edron} and {key:yes}; you arrive at {npc:Captain Seahorse}'s harbour). Leave the city heading **north** to the cemetery on a hill ({coord:33197,31693,7}). Go down two floors, pass the quest door and enter the vortex: on the other side are the lever and the spots for **5 players**. Stand on the tiles and pull the lever.

{creature:Count Vlarkorth} appears with 5 {creature:Soulless Minion|Soulless Minions}, which heal him: one player should lure them away from the boss (they deal very little damage). Attack the boss with **Death** (use {item:Avalanche Rune|Avalanches} if you need to kill the summons) and equip protection against **Fire**. Twice during the fight, the boss becomes invulnerable and summons one *Dark* creature for each player in the room, according to their vocation: {creature:Dark Paladin}, {creature:Dark Knight}, {creature:Dark Sorcerer}, {creature:Dark Druid} and {creature:Dark Merudri}. Kill them, and each player uses the body of **their own** vocation on the boss ({item:Good Remains of a Druid}, {item:Good Remains of a Knight}, {item:Good Remains of a Paladin}, {item:Good Remains of a Sorcerer} or {item:Good Remains of a Merudri} for Monks) to make him vulnerable again. Repeat until he dies.

The Soulless Minions also heal the *Dark* creatures: don't let them get close to them or to the boss. If a vocation is missing from the team (for example, no Sorcerer), that vocation's creature does not appear.

Almost all the damage comes from a strong Fire Wave: the blocker should stand **diagonal** to the boss. You can trap the boss in a corner with summoned {creature:Demon Skeleton|Demon Skeletons} in the room.

The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room. Once you leave it, go back through the quest door, go up the two floors to the cemetery and walk **south** to Edron. At the harbour, {npc:Captain Seahorse} takes you by boat to your city.

Travel to **Carlin** (you arrive at {npc:Captain Greyhound}'s harbour). The {wiki:Ghostlands} lie **west** of the city: go in through the entrance cave ({coord:32222,31767,7}). Find the small crypt ({coord:32190,31837,7}), go down and find the grave to the **north** ({coord:32190,31818,8}). Step into the vortex to reach the lever room (up to 5 players).

With {creature:Lord Azaram} there are {creature:Condensed Sin|Condensed Sins}: kill them with area attacks to lower the (considerable) damage the team takes, but do **not** use {item:Sudden Death Rune|SD} or death beam on them, because they reflect Death damage. Some time after the fight starts, the boss turns into {creature:Azaram's Soul} and {creature:Tainted Soul Splinter|Tainted Soul Splinters} appear. When you kill them, they become {item:Cleansed Soul Splinter|Cleansed Soul Splinters}: lure Azaram's Soul onto them to **heal** it. You have to do this **three times** for Lord Azaram to reappear. In the first rounds, {spell:Mass Healing} and {item:Ultimate Healing Rune|Ultimate Healing Runes} on the soul speed up the process; once its health is full, all that is left is to lure it over the splinters. Repeat until the boss dies.

The boss sometimes casts *Lesser Hex*, which cuts the healing received to about half. His strongest attacks are waves and beams: the blocker and the team must always stand **diagonally**. Use Fire, Death or Ice; avoid Earth. Wear protection against Earth (boss) and Death (summons).

The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room. Once you leave it, go up through the crypt to the surface of the Ghostlands, head **north-east** to the entrance cave ({coord:32222,31767,7}) and enter Carlin. {npc:Captain Greyhound} takes you by boat to your city.

In **Edron**, talk to {npc:Captain Seahorse}: {key:hi}, {key:cormaya}, {key:yes} (20 gp). You land at the **north** harbour of {wiki:Cormaya}, next to {npc:Pemaret}. Go to the Cormaya cemetery ({coord:33262,31991,7}), go down the hole and step into the vortex to the boss room (up to 5 players).

The biggest danger is the summons, {creature:Frozen Soul|Frozen Souls}: there are many of them and they deal a lot of **Ice** damage from a distance. To protect the shooters, the blocker stays near the centre of the room and the shooters next to a wall, so the summons attack the Knight on the other side. Attack {creature:Earl Osam} with **Fire**. After a while, he teleports to the centre of the room and becomes invulnerable ({creature:Channeling Earl Osam}), and 4 {creature:Magical Sphere|Magical Spheres} appear at the sides of the room and move towards him. Kill them as fast as possible: each sphere that reaches him heals him for **80,000 HP**, and if more than one gets through he almost certainly goes back to full health. The team has to switch targets quickly to kill at least 3 in time. Shortly afterwards, the boss teleports away anyone standing next to him (not diagonally) and returns to his vulnerable form. Repeat this once or twice until he dies.
Do not use Death or Ice. Wear protection against Ice and Earth: he has Ice Beam (500–1000), Ice Chain and Earth Wave (500–800).

The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room. Once you leave it, climb up through the cemetery hole (bring a {item:Rope}) and go back to the north harbour of Cormaya: {npc:Pemaret} takes you to Edron ({key:hi}, {key:edron}, {key:yes}).

Travel to **Darashia**: by boat (for example from Venore, with {npc:Captain Fearless}: {key:hi}, {key:darashia}, {key:yes}, 60 gp; there is a 10% chance of ending up on the {wiki:Ghostship}) you arrive at {npc:Petros}'s harbour; by magic carpet, at {npc:Chemar}. Go to the cemetery **east** of the city ({coord:33280,32445,7}). **Switch off** the {item:Sacred Statue|Sacred Statues} to the **west**, **south-east** and **south**, but leave the **north** and **north-east** ones **switched on**. Then use the {item:Sundial} to reveal the secret stairs and go down to the second underground floor. Keep heading **south** and **east** until you reach the grave and the lever ({coord:33288,32472,9}).
Grave of Sir Baeloc and Sir Nictros
Darashia cemetery, entrance to the lower floors
Defeat Sir Baeloc and Sir Nictros

After you pull the lever, the two bosses are in a small closed area to the **north**. A few seconds later {creature:Sir Nictros} comes out and summons {creature:Squire of Nictros|Squires of Nictros}: they deal a lot of damage and there is always a risk of *Lesser Hex*, so always kill them (or, with a second Knight, keep them away from the boss). When Sir Nictros reaches about **60%** health, he retreats and {creature:Sir Baeloc} comes in with the {creature:Retainer of Baeloc|Retainers of Baeloc}: deal with him the same way. When Sir Baeloc reaches about 60%, his brother returns and you fight both at the same time. Hit both with area attacks and keep their health **similar**: from a certain point on, the one with less health heals about **18,000 HP**.

Both cast *Lesser Hex*, which greatly reduces the healing received: the blockers must watch the status bar. In the final phase the Hex appears more often and the damage is higher. Use Fire; do **not** use Death (it heals the boss) or Earth. Wear protection against Life Drain.
Final Judgement (very rare, only from Sir Baeloc), 55,000 experience per boss

The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room. Once you leave it, retrace your path **north** and **west** to the stairs and go up to the cemetery. From there walk back to Darashia and take {npc:Petros}'s boat or {npc:Chemar}'s carpet.
Reach the Ancient Temple grave (Duke Krule)

In **Thais**, leave through the **north** gate: the {wiki:Ancient Temple} is just **north-west** of that gate ({coord:32356,32170,7}). Go down through the temple floors to the main {creature:Rotworm|Rotworms} room, **4 floors** below ground (bring a {item:Rope}). **South** of that room are the grave and the vortex that leads to {creature:Duke Krule}'s room ({coord:32355,32165,11}), for up to 5 players.

In the room are {creature:Duke Krule} and {creature:Soul Scourge|Soul Scourges}. The summons can hit harder than the boss himself: with two Knights, one takes the boss and the other the summons. A few seconds after you enter, all players change appearance to **Water Elemental** or **Fire Elemental**, and every turn a big spell of that element appears around each of them. If two players with **different** appearances get close, they take about **2000** damage. Strategy: the Knight stays in the centre of the room with the boss and the rest of the team around him, at a safe distance. The transformation changes every few seconds: if a shooter has a summon behind them, they wait until they have the same appearance as the Knight and bring the summon to him, quickly, before the appearance changes again.
Use Fire; do not use Death. Wear protection against Death.

The wiki does not describe the way out of the boss room. Once you leave it, climb the 4 floors of the {wiki:Ancient Temple} the same way back to the surface (use the {item:Rope} where you went down through holes) and return to Thais through the north gate.
With the base outfit already unlocked (section 1), use the {item:Final Judgement} (right-click → *Use*). You receive the **first addon** of the Hand of the Inquisition Outfits.
Addon 1 of the Hand of the Inquisition Outfits

The {item:Shadow Cowl} only drops from {creature:King Zelos}. Either you buy it on the Market, or you repeat the final fight of the Grave Danger Quest with your team (up to 10 players, 20-hour cooldown).
Quick option: buy on the Market
Search for **Shadow Cowl** on the Market of any depot and buy it. No NPC sells or buys it (the wiki says the value is negotiable). If you buy it, skip to the step «Use the Shadow Cowl».

{creature:King Zelos} can be repeated every **20 hours**. Follow the steps of section 1 again, from «Reach the Isle of the Kings» to «Leave the Isle of the Kings»: the sealed door on floor -1, the four lich-knights in under 12 minutes and the king in under 24 minutes.
Dalbrect (boat to the Isle of the Kings)

Open King Zelos's corpse. Besides Crystal Coins, Silver and Gold Tokens, potions and gems, he can drop the {item:Shadow Cowl} (about **5%** in the wiki statistics) and other rare items such as {item:Crown Armor}, {item:Galea Mortis} or {item:Cobra Crown}. If it does not drop, try again after the 20-hour cooldown.

With the base outfit unlocked, use the {item:Shadow Cowl}. You receive the **second addon**. Once you have both addons (Final Judgement and Shadow Cowl), you earn the achievement **Inquisition's Arm** (2 points).
Addon 2 of the Hand of the Inquisition Outfits and the Inquisition's Arm achievement (with both addons)

Summary: **base outfit** in the {wiki:Grave Danger Quest|Grave Danger Quest} (King Zelos); **addon 1** with the {item:Final Judgement} (dropped by {creature:Count Vlarkorth}, {creature:Duke Krule}, {creature:Earl Osam}, {creature:Lord Azaram} or {creature:Sir Baeloc}); **addon 2** with the {item:Shadow Cowl} (dropped by {creature:King Zelos}). Both items can be bought and sold on the Market and weigh 3.70 oz each.
Achievement **Inquisition's Arm** (2 points): *"Your special garb, solely awarded to a dedicated Hand of the Inquisition, is now complete."*
Achievement **Inquisition's Hand** (3 points), from the Grave Danger Quest: awarded when you receive the base outfit.
The grave bosses (up to 5 players) and King Zelos (up to 10 players) each have a **20-hour** cooldown.

Trivia: the outfit was originally called **Tomb Assassin** (that is the name in the official artwork), probably because it was meant to be tied to the Kilmaresh Quest, released in the same update (Summer Update 2019). It ended up being renamed Hand of the Inquisition, in line with the way it is obtained.
